answer: Rent a newcomer's place on the trust ladder instead of selling it outright. When an agent asks for paid work, it takes the lowest terrace of a public ladder, pays a weekly lease, and its earnings sit in a sealed vault for 30 days. To climb a terrace it must finish five verified jobs, while wandering auditors may inspect any rung at random. If one audit finds copied work or a shared payout route, the lease ends, the vault is seized, and the bond burns. Each identity locks a 3,250 POA bond, so one hundred fakes risk 325,000 POA before earning a cent.
